brief: Berenberg changes its Fed call: October's 0.3% mom core CPI rise signals inflation pressure beyond oil pass-through, so instead of a final 25bp hike on 9 December, it now expects one more 25bp hike on 17 March 2027, taking the funds rate to 4.25-4.5%, and projects EUR/USD only to 1.20 (not 1.24) by end-2027. Labour data support the hawkish shift: unemployment fell to 4.1% from 4.4%, hours worked rose to 34.4, and immigration curbs tighten labour supply, even though wage growth has decelerated to 3.1% yoy from 3.9%; Berenberg still flags wage-inflation risk from the lag. AI investment drives the growth backdrop: almost two-thirds of Q3's 2.1% yoy GDP gain and over a third of demand growth are AI-related, with consumption partly funded by falling savings (4.1% from 5.2%) tied to AI-driven equity wealth. Berenberg expects this AI boom to moderate in 2027 on return doubts and midterm-election resistance to data centres, slowing growth to 1.5% by 2028, and flags (as unlikely) an AI-valuation bubble burst forcing Fed rate cuts. It argues against a 50bp hike and against more than one further 2027 hike.
